Interiors of crockery may be warm white. Each illustration is completely separate, never touches another, with generous clear gutters. EXACTLY 4 equal columns by 4 equal rows; read row-major. Center one complete subject in each occupied cell and keep at least 15% of each cell clear at every edge. Use the available cell space to show useful detail; final presentation sizes will be assigned later. No perspective scene, no shared tabletop, no cell borders. Keep all objects completely within their own cell. Show no unrelated decoration. CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): Millstone. Small hand-operated pair of round stone grinding discs with central opening and projecting wooden crank. Essential visible cues: Two heavy stone discs and grinding aperture..
CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): Water. Clear glass water carafe, liquid visible only through faint contour and light reflections. Essential visible cues: Colorless transparent liquid; ordinary name still identifies contents..
CELL 4 (row 1, column 4): Apples. One red-green apple and a cut half with visible seeds. Essential visible cues: Apple profile, short stem and five-seed core..
CELL 5 (row 2, column 1): Fruit press. Compact wooden screw fruit press with basket, spindle and catching spout. Essential visible cues: Large screw over slatted fruit basket; distinguish from churn..
CELL 6 (row 2, column 2): Soaked grain. Bowl of visibly swollen whole kernels sitting in a shallow clear pool. Essential visible cues: Whole kernels remain discrete under water..
CELL 7 (row 2, column 3): Porridge. Bowl of thick cooked oats with coarse curved spoon furrow. Essential visible cues: Cooked swollen cereal texture; no fruit pieces..
CELL 8 (row 2, column 4): Fruit porridge. Low ceramic breakfast bowl of coarse creamy oats with prominent red-skinned apple pieces. Essential visible cues: Visible oats and fruit pieces together..
CELL 9 (row 3, column 1): Flour. Small open folded paper sack with fine off-white flour mound at its mouth and a little spill. Essential visible cues: Powdery matte flour; sack is a handling convention, not a chemical test..
CELL 10 (row 3, column 2): Dough. Pale compact kneaded dough ball with an uneven fold seam and lightly floury underside. Essential visible cues: One cohesive raw ball; no bubbles, layers or baked crust..
CELL 11 (row 3, column 3): Flatbread. Two thin irregular round breads, one folded to expose a soft pale interior. Essential visible cues: Thin blistered discs, no loaf height..
CELL 12 (row 3, column 4): Bread knife. Long serrated bread knife with dark wooden handle, blade fully visible. Essential visible cues: Saw teeth along long blade, distinct from pastry cutting wheel..
CELL 13 (row 4, column 1): Rolling pin. Long plain wooden rolling pin with two handles. Essential visible cues: Broad cylinder and handles, no blade or wire..
CELL 14 (row 4, column 2): Cutting wheel. Small fluted metal pastry wheel with short wooden handle. Essential visible cues: Circular scalloped cutting disc on handle..
CELL 15 (row 4, column 3): Whisk. Full balloon whisk with dark handle and individually legible looping metal wires. Essential visible cues: Wire balloon cage, not solid spoon or pestle..
CELL 16 (row 4, column 4): Straining cloth. Loose square of muslin with irregular corners, its middle lifted into a shallow draped pouch. Essential visible cues: Visible fabric weave and folds, no rigid vessel..
